partners.mechanism_chain: Loss-of-function variant in SLC16A1 (rs) —DISRUPTS→ SLC16A1 (HGNC:10922); SLC16A1 (HGNC:10922) —DISRUPTS→ Monocarboxylate Transport (GO:0015073); Monocarboxylate Transport (GO:0015073) —DECREASES→ Lactate (CHEBI:15077); Monocarboxylate Transport (GO:0015073) —DECREASES→ Ketone bodies (CHEBI:17472); Lactate (CHEBI:15077) —LEADS_TO→ Metabolic Myopathy (HP:0003670); Ketone bodies (CHEBI:17472) —LEADS_TO→ Ketoacidosis (HP:0001977). Loss-of-function variants in SLC16A1 disrupt the function of the monocarboxylate transporter 1 (MCT1). This leads to impaired transport of lactate out of muscle cells, causing metabolic myopathy (Disease A). It also impairs the transport of ketone bodies, contributing to ketoacidosis (Disease B). The shared convergence node is the disrupted monocarboxylate transport pathway, affecting both lactate and ketone body homeostasis.

partners.mechanism_chain: SLC16A1 (HGNC:11059) —DISRUPTS→ Lactate (CHEBI:15361); Lactate (CHEBI:15361) —LEADS_TO→ Myopathy (HP:0003198); UGT1A1 (HGNC:12225) —DISRUPTS→ Bilirubin conjugation pathway (REACT:764744); Bilirubin (CHEBI:17677) —BINDS→ Bilirubin conjugation pathway (REACT:764744); Bilirubin conjugation pathway (REACT:764744) —DECREASES→ Unconjugated Bilirubin (CHEBI:17677); Unconjugated Bilirubin (CHEBI:17677) —LEADS_TO→ Severe neonatal jaundice (HP:0011316). Loss-of-function mutations in SLC16A1 impair lactate transport, leading to intracellular lactate accumulation and myopathy. Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in UGT1A1 disrupt the bilirubin conjugation pathway, causing the accumulation of unconjugated bilirubin and severe neonatal jaundice. Both diseases, despite affecting different primary genes, converge on the disruption of critical metabolic pathways essential for cellular homeostasis and waste product clearance, ultimately leading to distinct but severe clinical phenotypes.
